Creates a 20-foot-high wall of elemental energy covering up to one 10-foot square per caster level. Choose acid, cold, electricity or fire at casting; the spell gains that descriptor, and any thrown weapon or piece of ammunition fired through the wall deals an extra 1d6 damage of that type on top of its normal damage. Melee weapons and untossed items are unaffected. You may restrict the wall to ranged weapons travelling in one chosen direction, which halves the duration.

augmenting-wall.notes: The extra 1d6 has no fixed damage type — acid, cold, electricity or fire is chosen at casting — so a damage spec would have to invent one of the four. It also fires per weapon that crosses the wall, not once at a target. Duration is omitted: the corpus says 'rounds/2 levels', and the shared duration shape can only express a whole amount per caster level, with no divisor. That gap is worth the orchestrator's attention — a rate of one unit per N levels is common.

Masks and rewrites a willing creature's or object's aura against read aura and analyze aura, changing all four aura types in one casting. Alignment: shift the apparent alignment up to one step on each axis (never to a diametric opposite) and its apparent power up or down by up to half your level in steps. Emotion: show any emotional colours you like, so nobody gains an aura-based bonus on Bluff, Diplomacy, Intimidate or Sense Motive against the target. Health: fake wounds, poison, disease, conditions and ki or similar resources within the target's normal range. Magic: register as nonmagical, as a magic item you name, or as the subject of a spell you name, masking every magic aura at once. An examiner using identify recognises the fake and sees the truth with a successful Will save, and an overwhelming item aura cannot be altered at all.

A 20-foot emanation that drains your own kind. Each round a creature starts its turn in the area sharing your creature type and at least one of your subtypes, it must make a Fortitude save or take 1d4 damage, and you gain that many temporary hit points (maximum 10 + your caster level), which vanish when the spell ends. While you hold at least 5 of those temporary hit points you have a +1 competence bonus on attack rolls, saving throws and skill checks; at 15 or more the bonus becomes +2.

aura-of-cannibalism.notes: Not converted to specs on purpose. The 1d4 repeats every round a qualifying creature starts its turn in the aura, and the vocabulary has no repeating-damage type; the temporary hit points are equal to damage actually dealt, which is not a number the spell states; and the +1/+2 competence bonus is gated on how many temporary hit points you are currently holding, a condition no spec can test. Emitting the bonus flat would grant it from the moment of casting, when the spell grants it only once you have drained someone.

There is no way in the vocabulary to say a bonus that scales with caster level — `scaling` only describes damage and healing dice. That is a real gap: caster-level-sized bonuses are common, and writing +1 here with a note would silently under-apply the spell at every level above 1.

Creates an identical copy of you and everything you wear and carry, anywhere within range; you exist in two places at once. Both may take free actions, and a body that has not moved may take a 5-foot step or move its speed once as a free action. Attacks, spells and effects treat the two as one person, applying the worse case — one save and one lot of damage from a fireball covering both, and both paralyzed if either fails against hold person. They count as a single creature for effects that target a number of creatures, but as separate creatures for flanking and cover, and not as two creatures for teamwork feats or effects that can only target someone other than yourself. A magical restraint on a living creature. It gets an initial Will save only if its Hit Dice are at least half your caster level, and setting a release condition raises that DC by 2. Up to six assistants may help: each casting suggestion adds 1 to your caster level for this binding, and each casting a dominate spell on a suitable target adds a third of that assistant's level; their own saves and spell resistance are irrelevant. You may set any reasonable triggering condition that releases the creature, based on name, identity, alignment or observable actions — never on level, class, Hit Dice or hit points — and it cannot be changed after casting. Choose one of six versions at casting. Chaining: restraints generating antipathy against all who approach except you, 1 year per caster level, confined to the spot, needs a chain long enough to wrap the creature three times. Slumber: comatose up to 1 year per caster level without food, drink or ageing, DC -1, needs a jar of sand or rose petals, a sleep effect. Bound slumber: both at once, 1 month per caster level, DC -2, a sleep effect. Hedged prison: permanently confined to an area it cannot leave, DC -3, consumes a tiny golden cage worth 100 gp. Metamorphosis: gaseous but for its head, held in a container, aware and able to speak but unable to leave, attack or use any ability, permanent, no need to breathe, eat, drink or age, DC -4. Minimus containment: shrunk to an inch or less inside a gem or jar, permanent, the same needs suspended, DC -4. Casting further bindings over the first three versions prolongs them, but the target then gets a save at the end of the first spell's duration even if it was denied one initially, and a success breaks every binding on it. Dispel magic cannot touch a binding, though antimagic field and mage's disjunction affect it normally, and a bound extraplanar creature cannot be sent home by dismissal or banishment.

effects.target: An invisible field lets weapons and natural attacks reach you but fouls them on the way back. When a melee attack hits you, make a caster level check against the attacker's CMD; on a success its weapon or limb is stuck to you as if affixed. It may drop a trapped weapon and walk away, but if it attacked with part of its body, or refuses to let go, it gains the grappled condition — you do not, since no part of you is holding it. On each of your later turns you may spend a standard action on a fresh caster level check against its CMD to maintain the grapple, taking any usual grappling action; pinning it makes you grappled too. On its turn it may escape with a combat maneuver or Escape Artist check against this spell's save DC. You may attack and cast normally while the field holds, but not make ranged weapon attacks, and only one limb or weapon can be snared at a time — a second hit forces you to choose which.

blade-snare.notes: The grappled condition lands on whoever attacks you, only after a caster level check beats its CMD, so it is retributive and conditional rather than something the spell applies to a target.

effects.target: A spirit of force hovers about your fists or melee weapons. Whenever you voluntarily take a penalty on melee attack rolls through a feat or maneuver — charging, fighting defensively, Power Attack — the spirit cuts that total penalty by 1, and by a further 1 for every 5 caster levels, never below a penalty of 0. Only voluntary penalties are reduced. The spirit cannot be attacked or harmed physically, though disintegrate, dispel magic, a rod of cancellation or a sphere of annihilation affects it, and its AC against touch attacks is 10 + your Dexterity modifier.

blade-tutor-s-spirit.notes: The reduction scales with caster level and cancels a penalty rather than adding a bonus, so it is not a combat_mod — emitting +1 to attack would give the bonus even when no voluntary penalty was taken.

effects.target: Move up to 30 feet in a straight line in any direction without provoking attacks of opportunity, and make one melee attack at your highest base attack bonus against any single creature you are adjacent to at any point along the way.

You leave a cascade of images behind you. You gain a circumstance bonus on that attack roll equal to your Intelligence or Charisma modifier, whichever is higher. You must end the movement in an unoccupied square, and the spell fails if no such space lies along the path. It works with any melee weapon.

bladed-dash.notes: The attack bonus is the size of an ability modifier, which a modifier spec's amount cannot hold.

effects.target: Move up to 30 feet in a straight line in any direction without provoking attacks of opportunity, and make one melee attack at your highest base attack bonus against every creature you pass — no creature more than once.

As bladed dash: a circumstance bonus on each attack roll equal to your Intelligence or Charisma modifier, whichever is higher, you must end in an unoccupied square, and the spell fails if none is available along the path.

Every nonevil creature in the 40-foot spread suffers effects set by its Hit Dice against your caster level, cumulative and concurrent, with one Will save applied to all of them. Hit Dice equal to your caster level: dazed. Up to caster level -1: weakened and dazed. Up to caster level -5: paralyzed, weakened and dazed. Up to caster level -10: killed, paralyzed, weakened and dazed. Dazed means no actions for 1 round, defending normally, save negates. Weakened means Strength down by 2d6 for 2d4 rounds, save for half. Paralyzed means paralyzed and helpless for 1d10 minutes, reduced by a save to 1 round. Killed means living creatures die and undead are destroyed, save negates — and a creature that saves against the killing takes 3d6 damage + 1 point per caster level, maximum +25, instead. If you are on your home plane, nonevil extraplanar creatures in the area are also banished home for at least 24 hours whether or not they heard you, negated by a Will save at -4. Creatures with more Hit Dice than your caster level are unaffected.
Cast from a 40-foot-radius spread centred on you; only nonevil creatures are affected.

blasphemy.notes: Deliberately not converted. Every outcome, including the 3d6 + 1/level, is gated on the target's Hit Dice measured against caster level, which no spec can test — and the 3d6 belongs only to creatures in the 'killed' band that save, not to everyone who saves. Emitting it as the spell's damage would hit a creature that was merely dazed. The paralysis and the Strength loss are likewise band-specific.

effects.target: A 60-foot line of hurricane-force wind at 90 mph, functioning as gust of wind except that every creature in the area is treated as one size category smaller when working out how the wind affects it — one further category smaller for every 4 caster levels past 7th, to a maximum of three categories smaller at 15th level.

Choose one of two forms at casting. Bow: a longbow or shortbow sized for you, which you are proficient with; drawing it creates a +1 seeking brilliant energy arrow and it fires nothing else. A creature struck by one is surrounded by faerie fire and dazzled for 1 minute. This form ends once you have fired arrows equal to your caster level. Bridge: a ramp of light 5 feet wide and up to 10 feet long per caster level. Everyone on it is dazzled; allies gain a bonus equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum 1, on checks, saves and CMD to resist being moved off it against their will, and enemies take the same figure as a penalty.

blazing-rainbow.notes: Two alternative forms chosen at casting, and the bridge's bonus and penalty are the size of the caster's Wisdom modifier. Corpus duration is 'minutes/level or until discharged'; the per-level half is emitted and the arrow-count discharge described.

effects.target: Ability score drain you have taken from the Bleaching stops affecting your ability score modifiers. It does not undo the Bleaching's mark on your appearance, and does not stop you taking further ability penalties, dying, or becoming a bleachling.

bleaching-resistance.notes: It suspends the effect of drain already suffered rather than restoring points, which ability_restore would do — the drain is still there when the spell ends.

bleed.notes: The 1 point per round that follows is the ordinary dying rule, not damage this spell repeats, so only the single point the last line states is emitted. The creature can be stabilized again normally afterwards.

effects.target: Cast as an immediate action when an attack roll would hit you, or when you are in an area that allows you a Reflex save, on your animal companion, eidolon, familiar or mount. Against an attack roll, the companion takes the damage in your place even if the roll would not have beaten its own AC. Against a Reflex-save area, it instead gives you cover (+2 on the Reflex save) if it is your size or smaller, or improved cover (+4 and improved evasion against that effect) if it is larger; it automatically fails its own Reflex save, though its own improved evasion and similar still apply.

bleed-for-your-master.notes: The damage redirected onto the companion is whatever the triggering attack deals — a number this spell never states — so no damage spec is emitted. The +2 or +4 cover bonus goes to the caster, not to the companion the spell targets, so it is narrated rather than emitted as a save_mod that would land on the wrong creature.

effects.note: Targets a mythic creature.

on_failure.target: Every path ability, feat, spell and other effect the target uses costs 1 more point of mythic power than usual.

effects.target: A touched slashing melee weapon can open a bleeding wound. As a free action when it hits a living creature, the wielder discharges the spell to add 1 point of bleed to the weapon's base damage. The bleeding is hard to close: add your spellcasting ability modifier — Wisdom for a cleric, and so on — to the DC required to stop it.

bleeding-strike.notes: The spell's target is the weapon; the bleed lands on whatever living creature the weapon later strikes, once the wielder chooses to discharge it. A bleed spec here would bleed the wielder. The DC to stop it is also raised by an ability modifier, which the stopped_by field can only state in words.

Attempt Stealth checks with no cover or concealment, so long as you move no more than half your base speed.

Your colouring and your equipment's shift to match your surroundings. Move more than half your base speed on your turn and you gain nothing from the spell until the start of your next turn. Making an attack ends the spell, as invisibility.
stealth

effects.target: Use Stealth even while being observed, so long as you do not move.

The creature takes on the look of a statue, furniture, a tree, a bush, a rock or another object of about its size, as you choose. Its armour blends into the illusory shape and its armour check penalty on Stealth is negated for the duration. The spell ends the moment the target moves at all.

blend-with-surroundings.notes: No bonus type is stated for the +20, so it is untyped. Negating the armour check penalty cancels a number that varies with the armour worn, which no modifier spec can express.

effects.target: an army's OM and Morale checks

bless-army.notes: A mass combat spell: the target is an army, not a creature, and OM and Morale are army statistics with no entry in any vocabulary. Duration omitted because the corpus says '1 battle', and the duration units are round, minute, hour and day — a battle is none of them. That is a real gap for the mass combat spells.

effects.target: Imbues a touched flask of water — 1 pint — with positive energy, turning it into holy water.

The touched weapon counts as having a +1 enhancement bonus purely for beating the damage reduction of evil creatures and striking evil incorporeal ones, without granting an actual enhancement bonus, and becomes good-aligned for overcoming damage reduction — overriding and suppressing any other alignment it had. Individual arrows or bolts may be transmuted, but a bow so treated passes nothing to its arrows. Every critical threat against an evil foe is automatically confirmed, except on a weapon that already has a magical critical effect such as keen or vorpal.

bless-weapon.notes: The prose is explicit that the +1 is not an actual enhancement bonus, only a figure used against damage reduction, so emitting a combat_mod would give the weapon a bonus the spell says it does not grant.

effects.target: Count as armed even when unarmed, so unarmed strikes provoke no attacks of opportunity.
Choose whether each unarmed strike deals lethal or nonlethal damage.

If the target already counts as armed when unarmed — from the monk's unarmed strike or Improved Unarmed Strike — it instead gains a +1 enhancement bonus on attack and damage rolls with its unarmed strikes, and those strikes count as good-aligned weapons for overcoming damage reduction.

blessed-fist.notes: The +1 is conditional on the target already having the ability the spell would otherwise grant, and applies only to unarmed strikes. A combat_mod on attack and damage would give it to every target and to every weapon.

effects.target: saving throws against fear and death effects
At any point while the spell lasts the target may end it as a swift action for a burst of healing energy: it loses the saving throw bonus and is healed 1d8 + 1 point per caster level, maximum +10.

blessing-of-courage-and-life.notes: The healing is real and lands on the target, but only when the target spends a swift action to discharge the spell — never at casting. A heal spec would be rolled the moment the spell is cast, healing the target and leaving the buff running, which is the opposite of the trade the spell offers. `scaling` is omitted for the same reason: with no spec to attach to, it would only advertise healing the cast does not do.

effects.target: At the start of each of its turns, every affected ally picks one benefit for that round: increase its speed by 30 feet; stand up as a swift action without provoking; make one extra attack as part of a full attack at its highest base attack bonus; gain +2 on attack rolls and a +2 dodge bonus to AC and Reflex saves; or cast one spell of 2nd level or lower as though enlarged, extended, silent or still. None of it is cumulative with similar effects such as haste or a speed weapon, and none of it grants an actual extra action, so it cannot buy a second spell or another action in the round. Does not stack with haste.

blessing-of-fervor.notes: Five alternatives, re-chosen every round by each ally for itself. Emitted as specs they would all apply at once and for the whole duration, which is neither what the spell grants nor how long it grants it for.

effects.target: End the spell as a swift action to gain a +20-foot enhancement bonus to your base speed for 1 round per whole minute of duration remaining.
You gain a +1 luck bonus per 6 caster levels, minimum +1 and maximum +3, to your CMD and on saving throws against spells and traps that would move you or impede your movement.

blessing-of-liberty.notes: The bonus scales with caster level between +1 and +3, so no fixed amount states it: emitting +1 would be wrong from 6th level up. The speed burst is not emitted as a `speed` spec either — it costs the spell, and its length is measured in whole minutes of duration left over.

effects.target: saving throws against fear effects
After failing a saving throw against fear, end the spell as an immediate action to reroll that save with a +4 morale bonus — you must take the new result even if it is worse.
If the target has the fearless racial trait it is immune to fear instead of gaining the +2.

blessing-of-luck-and-resolve.notes: The immunity replaces the bonus and only for targets with the fearless racial trait, a condition no spec can test, so it is narrated rather than emitted alongside the +2 as though a target got both.

effects.target: saving throws against fear effects
After failing a saving throw against fear, end the spell as an immediate action to reroll that save with a +4 morale bonus — you must take the new result even if it is worse.
Affects one creature per caster level, no two more than 30 feet apart. A target with the fearless racial trait is immune to fear instead of gaining the +2.

blessing-of-luck-and-resolve-mass.notes: Numbers taken from blessing of luck and resolve, which this spell functions as; the only stated difference is the number of targets.

blessing-of-the-watch.notes: The two modifiers are copied from bless, which this spell functions as and which states '+1 morale bonus on attack rolls and on saving throws against fear effects' in its own prose. The save_mod is written on Will to match the already-converted bless exactly rather than diverge from the spell this one inherits from.

effects.target: The target weapon becomes pure blightburn. It works as normal, but any creature touching it, or struck by it, takes 2d6 fire damage each round it stays in contact. The weapon also emanates radiation causing blightburn sickness, as the disease, in a 10-foot radius and at this spell's save DC.

blightburn-weapon.notes: The 2d6 repeats every round of contact and lands on whoever holds or is struck by the weapon — the spell's target is the weapon itself, so a damage spec would burn the wielder once at casting. `element` is set to fire because the prose names fire damage and the corpus derived no element; note the spell carries no [fire] descriptor of its own.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: Fortitude negates. Targets one living creature; the effect is permanent but dismissible.

on_failure.target: The subject is rendered either blinded or deafened, whichever you chose when you cast the spell.

blindness-deafness.notes: Both blinded and deafened are in the condition vocabulary, but the spell inflicts one of them at the caster's choice and there is no way to say 'one of these, chosen at casting'. Emitting both apply_condition specs would blind and deafen the same creature, which the spell never does, and picking one would be inventing the caster's decision. This is the cleanest example in the partition of a gap worth closing — an exclusive-choice branch would make a core spell executable.

effects.target: Your blood hardens like iron on contact with air. Each time you take at least 5 points of piercing or slashing damage, your armour gains a +1 enhancement bonus to your AC; ordinary clothing counts as armour granting no AC bonus for this purpose. The bonus stacks with itself to a maximum of +5. The spell does nothing underwater or anywhere without air.

blood-armor.notes: The bonus does not exist when the spell is cast — it is earned +1 at a time by taking 5 or more points of piercing or slashing damage, up to +5. A combat_mod would hand the caster armour they have not bled for yet.
